definitions.explanation: Mochi that has been grilled or toasted, typically over a flame or in a toaster oven, causing it to puff up and develop a crispy exterior.
Jealousy, particularly the kind felt in romantic or close personal relationships. Often used in a somewhat lighthearted or teasing way.

examples.japanese: {焼|や}き{餅|もち}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{食|た}べる→食べる：00396_taberu⟧。
⟦お{正月|しょうがつ}→お正月：05586_oshougatsu⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{焼|や}き{餅|もち}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{焼|や}いた→焼く：01123_yaku⟧。
examples.english: I grilled mochi on New Year's.

examples.japanese: ⟦{醤油|しょうゆ}→醤油：01056_shouyu⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦つけた→つける：00562_tsukeru⟧{焼|や}き{餅|もち}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{一番|いちばん}→一番：01140_ichiban⟧⟦{好|す}き→好き：02355_suki⟧だ。
examples.english: I like grilled mochi with soy sauce the best.

⟦そんな→そんな：01645_sonna⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{焼|や}き{餅|もち}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{焼|や}かないで→焼く：01123_yaku⟧、⟦ただ→ただ：01613_tada⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{友達|ともだち}→友達：01478_tomodachi⟧だ⟦よ→よ：09475_yo⟧。
examples.english: Don't be so jealous — we're just friends.

notes:
This word has two distinct meanings connected by a pun on the verb ⟦{焼|や}く→焼く：01123_yaku⟧ (to grill/burn). Sense 1 is literal grilled mochi. Sense 2 uses the expression {焼|や}き{餅|もち}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{焼|や}く→焼く：01123_yaku⟧, which literally means "to grill grilled mochi" but idiomatically means "to be jealous."

USAGE:
The jealousy sense is most commonly used in the phrase {焼|や}き{餅|もち}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{焼|や}く→焼く：01123_yaku⟧. It tends to describe romantic jealousy and has a somewhat playful or teasing tone compared to the more serious ⟦{嫉妬|しっと}→嫉妬：05406_shitto⟧.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {焼|や}き{餅|もち}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{焼|や}く→焼く：01123_yaku⟧ — to be jealous (sense 2); to grill mochi (sense 1)
- {焼|や}き{餅|もち}{焼|や}き — a jealous person
- ⟦{醤油|しょうゆ}→醤油：01056_shouyu⟧{焼|や}き{餅|もち} — soy sauce grilled mochi

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{嫉妬|しっと}→嫉妬：05406_shitto⟧ — jealousy (stronger, more serious)
- {妬|ねた}む — to envy, to be jealous of (verb)
- ⟦{羨|うらや}ましい→羨ましい：02336_urayamashii⟧ — envious (less negative, more admiring)
